Under Review at CVPR 2027

Contacts Carry the Depth A Learned Flight Prior for Monocular 3D Soccer Ball Reconstruction

Ritabrata Chakraborty

School of Engineering and Applied Science, University of Pennsylvania

Paper (On Request) Supplementary (On Request) Code Interactive Demo Cite
AbstractMethodSetupResultsQualitativeDemoCitation

Abstract

From one camera, the 3D flight of a soccer ball is fixed only up to its depth along the viewing rays. On the Ball3D benchmark we measure where that depth comes from: removing the two contact anchors raises a physics fit's median broadcast error from 0.92 to 2.57 m, while an arc through the anchors alone, with no image fit, reaches 1.54 m. The contacts carry the depth; the image arc refines it. We therefore learn a flight prior for where the data are weak. ArcPrior, a 1.24M-parameter transformer over per-frame world rays, predicts four flight hypotheses with spreads, which a batched Levenberg–Marquardt solver refines under the benchmark's losses and the spread-weighted prior. With oracle contacts (annotated times, ground-truth heights), ArcPrior lowers the median broadcast error of the benchmark's optimiser, Ball3D, from 0.955 to 0.848 m (pHolm = .001). On full broadcast flights lift terms alone match this; the prior pays off on static views and on partially seen flights (3.72 vs 6.27 m for a physics-only fit). Its split-conformal 90 % error bounds cover 89–91 % of test flights and fall below the 10 m error cap from 80 % seen. From raw video with the SoccerNet-v3D detector and PnLCalib, the error rises to 1.68 m. Fine-tuning only their heads brings it to 0.905 m with ground-truth-checked labels and to 0.968 m with labels from our own fits, which need no 3D trajectory ground truth or dataset camera; neither beats Ball3D significantly. All results are cross-validated on one match with oracle contacts.

Method

Rays and ContactsOracle ContactsEach frame's camera and ball box give a ray through the bottom of the box and a box size. Every method in every scenario receives the same contacts: annotated contact times, contact type from the ground-truth height, and an anchor where the scenario's own ray reaches that height.
ArcPriorRay Tokens to HypothesesEach frame becomes one token; a learned query token pools the flight through six pre-norm transformer encoder layers, and an MLP maps it to K = 4 bounded flight hypotheses, each with spreads and a logit.
SolverRefinement and BoundsEach hypothesis is integrated by one batched, differentiable RK4 step per frame and refined by Levenberg–Marquardt under the benchmark's losses and the spread-weighted prior; the solver's covariance gives a per-flight predicted error Ω and split-conformal bounds.

Flight Model

A flight is the ball's motion between two contacts. It has ten parameters: start position and velocity, quadratic drag, lift and sidespin coefficients, and gravity. The benchmark's best monocular model, fitg, sets lift and sidespin to zero and fits gravity within 9.806 ± 3.5 m s−2, so within that range its image term alone cannot fix depth. ArcPrior fixes gravity and frees the lift and sidespin terms, so lift cannot be traded for gravity and curvature keeps a weak hold on depth.

ArcPrior

In the 1.24M-parameter network, each frame becomes one token in a flight-aligned frame, with its origin at the start anchor; rays remove the moving camera from what the network has to learn. Besides the ray geometry, a token holds the time from the start contact with Fourier features, the contact flags and end anchor, the log focal length, a size-based depth and the view. Time is never divided by the flight length, so a cut flight does not reveal its length.

Observability

At the solution, the Gauss–Newton covariance over the parameters that are not at a bound gives each flight a predicted error Ω. For split-conformal bounds we take, for each share of the flight seen, the 90 % quantile q of RMSE/Ω on the fold's validation block; the one-sided test bound is RMSE ≤ q Ω. ArcPrior-full is trained on whole flights and ArcPrior-cut on randomly cut flights.

Experimental Setup

398airborne flights of the LP match (broadcast and static cameras 01–05)
4 foldseach half split into two time blocks; every block is test once and validation once
3 seedsper fold; a flight's error is averaged over the seeds
1.24Mparameters in ArcPrior, trained on S1 flights only and applied unchanged in S2 and S3
ScenarioWhere the Rays Come From
S1Tracked detections and cameras of the benchmark
S2Video: YOLO ball detector (SoccerNet-v3D), tracker, PnLCalib MV
S3-supS2 with its heads fine-tuned on ground-truth-checked labels
S3-selfThe same heads fine-tuned on our own fits, no 3D ground truth
S3-LOCOS3-sup static heads trained without the tested camera

Camera 06, whose pitch fills only the lower half of its image, was excluded before training for its very different view angle. E-full is the capped full-flight RMSE and E-part its mean over 30–90 % seen. Baselines: Ball3D, the optimiser of Ball3D with fitg on the same inputs and contacts; LM-fitg, our solver with the fitg model and start, no network; SNv3D-size, per-frame depth from ball size (SoccerNet-v3D).
